NONE: › extremely violent, wild, or frightening
兇殘的；兇猛的；野性的
› very serious or cruel
無情的，冷酷的
› If an animal savages someone, it attacks them violently and causes serious injuries.
（動物）兇猛地攻擊，撕咬
› a person whose way of life is at a very early stage of development
野蠻人；未開化的人
› very large and severe
巨大的；嚴重的

example: a savage dog/beast
兇猛的狗／野獸
a brutal and savage attack
野蠻兇殘的攻擊
The child was savaged by a dog.
那個孩子被狗咬傷了。
Twelve thousand years ago, our ancestors were primitive savages living in caves.
12000年以前，我們的祖先生活在洞穴裡，是原始野蠻人。

NONE: › in a violent, cruel, or very severe way
野蠻地；殘酷地；兇暴地
› (acts of) cruel and violent behaviour
殘暴（行爲），兇殘（行徑）；獸性
› a large, flat area of land covered with grass, usually with few trees, that is found in hot countries, especially in Africa
（尤指非洲等熱帶國家的）稀樹草原
› a person with a high level of knowledge or skill, especially someone who is less able in other ways
（尤指在其他方面缺乏能力的）博學之士，學者，專家

example: There are musical savants who are very awkward physically - until they sit at the piano.
有些音樂專家平時舉止顯得不自然，但一旦坐在鋼琴面前就大不一樣。

T: B1 [ T ] to stop someone or something from being killed, injured, or destroyed

NONE: B1 to stop someone from being killed
使（某人）免遭殺害；救（某人）的性命
› informal to help someone escape from a difficult or unpleasant situation
幫助（某人）脫離困境（或窘境）

I or T: A2 [ I or T ] to keep something, especially money, for use in the future
A2 [ I or T ] to put information into a computer's memory or onto a computer disk
將（電腦上的資料）存檔，保存
B1 [ I or T ] to prevent time, money, or effort being wasted or spent

T: B2 [ T ] in football and similar games, to stop the ball from going into the goal when a player on the other team has kicked or hit it
（足球等球類運動中）救（球），阻止對方得（分）

NONE: › in football or similar games, when a player stops the ball from going into the goal when it is hit or kicked by a player from the other team
（足球等球類運動中）救（球），阻止對方得（分）
› but or except for
除…外

example: Wearing seat belts has saved many lives.
繫安全帶挽救了許多人的生命。
He fell in the river but his friend saved him from drowning.
他掉進河裡，不過他的朋友救了他的命。
He had to borrow money to save his business.
他只好借錢挽救自己的企業。
He was desperately trying to save their failing marriage.
他拼命努力，試圖挽救他們瀕臨破裂的婚姻。
We all need to do our part to save the planet.
我們都需要為拯救地球而出一份心力。
The former tennis champion was now serving to save the match (= to win the next point so that the other player did not win this part of the competition).
前網球冠軍正在發球爭取挽回頹勢。
Thanks for helping me with that report - you saved my life!
謝謝你幫助我完成那個報告——你真是幫了我大忙！
Tom's been saving his pocket money every week.
湯姆每週都把自己的零用錢存起來。
We're saving (up) for a new car.
我們正在存錢準備買一輛新車。
I save all my old letters in case I want to read them again.
我把過去所有的信件都保存下來，以便日後再讀。
Save me a place at your table, OK?
你坐的那張桌子幫我留個位子好嗎？
Don't forget to save your work regularly.
不要忘記經常存檔。
To save, press Control S.
存檔按Control和S鍵。
You'll save time if you take the car.
開車會省些時間。
[ + two objects ] Thanks for your help - it saved me a lot of work.
謝謝你的幫助——這省了我很多事。
[ + -ing verb ] I'll lend you a bag for your trip - it'll save you buying one.
我借給你一個旅行提袋——省得你專程再買一個。
informal Can you save it for later (= tell me your news later when I am less busy)?
你能等一下（在我不那麼忙的時候）再告訴我嗎？

The goalkeeper made a great save in the last minute of the game.
守門員在比賽的最後關頭有一次精彩的撲救。
They found all the lost documents save one.
除了其中有一份沒有找到之外，他們找到了所有丟失的文件。

NONE: A2 to keep money so that you can buy something with it in the future
儲蓄，存（錢）

example: It took me months to save up enough money to go travelling.
我用了幾個月的時間才存夠了錢去旅遊。
She's saving up for a new bike.
她正在存錢，想買一輛新腳踏車。

NONE: › to avoid using something so that you do not have to pay for it
節省，節約

example: It was a warm winter, so we saved on electricity.
那是一個暖冬，因此我們省了不少電。

NONE: › to help someone avoid getting into trouble
幫助（某人）避開麻煩
› to do something that prevents a likely defeat or failure
轉危爲安，扭轉頹勢

example: The team seemed to be heading for disaster until a late goal saved the day.
這支球隊似乎就要陷入絕境，直到後來憑藉一顆進球才扭轉頹勢。

NONE: › used to say that it is not worth talking to someone because they will not listen to you
不值得浪費唇舌；不必對牛彈琴

example: I don't know why I even try to talk to him - I might as well save my breath.
我不知道爲甚麽要浪費唇舌和他說話——最好還是不要對牛彈琴。

NONE: › to protect yourself from danger or difficulty, without trying to help other people
只管自己不顧他人
› to save money for a time when it might be needed unexpectedly
存錢以備不時之需；有備無患；未雨綢繆

example: Luckily she had saved some money for a rainy day.
幸好她未雨綢繆早有準備。

NONE: › something that you say when a difficult situation ends suddenly before you have to do or say something that you do not want to
救命鈴（某種困難局面突然結束時所說的話，假使局面持續下去，你就需要做不想做的事或說不想說的話）

example: Luckily my bus arrived before I had time to reply. Saved by the bell.
正當我要回答時，公車就到了，真是萬幸。

NONE: › a person who saves money regularly
儲蓄者
› something that makes it possible for you to use less of the stated thing
有助於節省…的事物

example: A washing machine is a great time-saver.
洗衣機能節省大量時間。
a money/energy saver
有助於省錢／節能的事物

NONE: B2 the money that you keep in an account in a bank or similar financial organization
存款，儲蓄金

C: C1 [ C ] an amount of money that you do not need to spend

NONE: › making it possible to use less of the stated thing
能節省…的；可以節約…的

example: He spent all his savings on an expensive car.
他花了自己所有的存款買了一輛昂貴的汽車。
You can make huge savings (= save a lot of money) by buying food in bulk.
大量購買食品能省下很多錢。
a time-saving recipe
省時間的竅門
a money-saving offer
便宜的報價
a labour-saving device
節省人力的裝置

NONE: › a good quality that something or someone has that stops it, him, or her from being completely bad
可取之處

example: The film's only/one saving grace is the excellent cinematography.
這部電影（唯一的／的一個）可取之處就是攝影很出色。

NONE: › an account in a bank or similar financial organization that earns interest
儲蓄帳戶

example: Compare
current account

NONE: › a business that lends you money if you want to buy a house, or pays you interest on money you invest there
房屋互助協會
› a bank that only offers accounts where your money earns interest
儲蓄銀行
› a person who saves someone from danger or harm
救助者；拯救者；救星
› in the Christian religion, a way of referring to Jesus
救世主（Jesus的另一種說法）
› a child who is born with particular genes that have been chosen in order to treat an older brother or sister who has a disease
兄姐救星（生來就有某些特殊基因的孩子，這些基因是經過特別選擇的，用於治療孩子罹患絕症的哥哥或姐姐）
› the ability to do and say the right thing in any social situation
隨機應變的能力；應付自如的社交能力

example: She possesses great savoir-faire.
她的社交能力極強。

NONE: › to enjoy food or an experience slowly, in order to enjoy it as much as possible
細品，享用（食物）
› pleasure and interest
樂趣；趣味；情趣
› a smell or taste, especially a pleasant one
（尤指美好的）氣味；味道，滋味

example: It was the first chocolate he'd tasted for over a year, so he savoured every mouthful.
這是他一年多來吃到的第一塊巧克力，因此他每一口都細細品嚐。
She felt that life had lost most of its savour.
她覺得生活失去了大部分樂趣。

NONE: › to have particular characteristics or qualities that make people think of something, especially something unpleasant
有（尤指不好的）特點；帶有…意味

example: His behaviour does rather savour of hypocrisy.
他的行爲相當虛僞。

NONE: › Savoury food is salty or spicy and not sweet in taste.
鹹的；辛辣的
› If you say that something is not savoury, you mean that it is not pleasant or socially acceptable.
令人愉快的；名聲好的；受歡迎的

example: a savoury dish/sauce/flavour
帶鹹味的一道菜／一種調料／一種味道
A pie can be sweet or savoury.
餡餅可以是甜的或鹹的。
That hotel doesn't have a very savoury reputation.
那家旅館的聲譽不太好。

NONE: › a type of cabbage with curly leaves
皺葉甘藍
› practical knowledge and ability
常識；實際能力

example: business savvy
專業知識
She hasn't got much savvy.
她的能力還不夠。
